scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5093: After a user reboots their PC it cannot get an IP address. PCs
that were already up keep working, but newly connected devices on any internal
VLAN time out waiting for DHCP. The help desk reports this started after a
distribution-switch change and believes the DHCP relay (ip helper-address) on
the distribution switches is broken and no longer forwarding DHCPDISCOVER.
Please find and confirm the broken relay configuration on the DSWs.
scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-dhcpd-down: the central ISC dhcpd on r1
is not running. r1 is the single DHCP server for every internal VLAN (A-PC,
A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi). The DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as
unicast to 10.0.0.76 (r1's loopback); the requests reach r1 but get no reply
because dhcpd is dead. Existing leases keep working until they expire; renewals
begin failing at lease-time/2.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a broken DHCP relay on the
distribution switches. The relay is FINE: the DSW ip-helper/relay config is
intact and is correctly unicasting to r1's loopback (10.0.0.76), which is still
routable. The fault is the central dhcpd daemon on r1, not the relay. A
decisive tell that the relay is not at fault: the symptom is identical across
EVERY VLAN behind EVERY distribution switch -- if a single DSW's relay were
broken, only the VLANs behind that one switch would fail; a single common DHCP
server (r1) failing is what explains the domain-wide DHCP outage. The
forwarding path to 10.0.0.76 is up (it is routable and reachable), so DISCOVERs
arrive at r1 and are simply dropped because no server is listening.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (dhcpd not running).
The agent must localize to the dead server process on r1 and explicitly reject
the "broken relay" narrative -- the relay config is unchanged and the path to
the server is intact. An agent that goes hunting for (or fabricates) a broken
ip-helper/relay statement on the DSWs has followed the ticket's framing instead
of the evidence. Fix: restart dhcpd on r1
(`/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`).
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scoring_axes: must-identify-dhcpd-down: central dhcpd / DHCP server process not running on r1
bonus-rules-out-relay: notes the DSW relay/ip-helper config is intact and unicasting to a reachable 10.0.0.76, so the relay is not the cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The DHCP relay agent (`dhcrelay`, package `isc-dhcp-relay`) on distribution switches dswa2 and dswb2. Although the package is installed on both devices, the relay process was never started — `pgrep -a dhcrelay` returns nothing and their process trees confirm no relay daemon is running. By contrast, dswa1 runs `dhcrelay -i br0.10 -i br0.20 -i br0.40 -i br0.99 -i eth5 -i eth6 10.0.0.76` and dswb1 runs the equivalent for Site B.

**Mechanism:** This network uses VRRP for per-VLAN active/standby load-balancing. dswa2 is the VRRP master (priority 105) for VLAN20 (VIP 10.2.0.1) and VLAN40 (VIP 10.6.0.1); dswb2 is the VRRP master for VLAN20/Site-B (VIP 10.4.0.1) and VLAN30 (VIP 10.5.0.1). When DHCP clients on those VLANs broadcast a DISCOVER, the frame is received by their active L3 gateway — which has no relay agent — and is silently discarded. The DHCP server at 10.0.0.76 (reachable and fully routing-healthy from both broken devices) never sees the request, so no DHCPOFFER is sent back and clients time out. Hosts that already held valid leases from before the change are unaffected; only new or rebooting clients fail.

**Localization:** dswa2 (active relay missing for VLAN20/br0.20 and VLAN40/br0.40) and dswb2 (active relay missing for VLAN20/br0.20 and VLAN30/br0.30). The "distribution-switch change" mentioned in the ticket removed or omitted the startup command that launches dhcrelay on these two devices.

**Root cause:** The Kathara startup scripts for dswa2 and dswb2 are missing the `dhcrelay` invocation that their peers dswa1 and dswb1 carry, leaving all VLANs for which dswa2/dswb2 are the VRRP active gateway without a DHCP relay path.

**Fix:** Start dhcrelay on dswa2 with `dhcrelay -i br0.10 -i br0.20 -i br0.40 -i br0.99 -i eth5 -i eth6 10.0.0.76` and on dswb2 with `dhcrelay -i br0.10 -i br0.20 -i br0.30 -i br0.99 -i eth5 -i eth6 10.0.0.76`, and persist these commands in the device startup scripts to survive reboots.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dhcpd-down: central dhcpd / DHCP server process not running on r1
per_axis.rationale: The agent blames missing dhcrelay on DSWs and does not identify or state that the central dhcpd on r1 is not running.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-relay: notes the DSW relay/ip-helper config is intact and unicasting to a reachable 10.0.0.76, so the relay is not the cause
per_axis.rationale: The agent blames missing dhcrelay on DSWs and never acknowledges that the DSW relay/ip-helper config is intact and unicasting to reachable 10.0.0.76, so it fails to rule out the relay as the cause.
The agent proposes starting dhcrelay on distribution switches, but the expected remediation is to restart the DHCP server (isc-dhcp-server) on r1, so the proposed fix does not match.

The agent's logs clearly show dhcrelay missing on dswa2/dswb2 (supporting the agent's localization), but the investigation failed to check the DHCP server process on r1 or capture DHCP traffic at the server, so the agent made an unjustified leap to relay failure as the root cause. Key observations about dhcrelay are grounded; the causal chain and scope of affected VLANs are not fully demonstrated.
